Krea 2 Turbo on Mac: files, RAM and published times

Krea 2 Turbo is the 8-step distilled text-to-image checkpoint of Krea 2. Commercial use is allowed only below USD $1,000,000 in annual revenue under the Krea 2 Community License.

Krea · Updated 2026-10-24
Answer

Krea 2 Turbo runs on a Mac with 32 GB or more. A published run on M1 Max · 32 GB used the Turbo MLX mixed-4/8 build (source, 2026-07-08).

Does it fit your NVIDIA GPU's VRAM?

Runs · Stated means the linked model card, app maker or NVIDIA says a GPU with that much VRAM runs the model; Runs · Published names the card of a dated run. Fits with offload means the main model weights fit in VRAM with a 15% margin but the full set does not: the text encoder and VAE run from system RAM, which is slower. Exceeds VRAM means even the main weights are too large for the card. Mac runs never count here.

Which Mac software routes are listed?

  • ComfyUI-Krea2-MLX

    Community · v0.4.0

    Formats: mlx. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    Unofficial ComfyUI node pack that runs Krea 2 Turbo in-process on MLX. It keeps one model resident and does not plug into the native KSampler.

    Sources: ComfyUI-Krea2-MLX README

  • Diffusers

    Official

    Formats: safetensors, gguf. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    Runs on the PyTorch mps device on Mac and CUDA on NVIDIA. GGUF loads through from_single_file on the model class, not the pipeline. Resident size is the sum of the weights, an upper bound.

    Sources: Diffusers MPS guide · Diffusers GGUF guide

  • mflux

    Community · 0.23.0

    Formats: safetensors. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    MLX-native runner. It reads the original Hugging Face weights and quantizes them while loading (--quantize 3, 4, 5, 6 or 8). --low-ram lowers memory use at a performance cost.

    Install with uv

    uv tool install --upgrade mflux

    Sources: mflux README, install · mflux pyproject · mflux common README, quantization

  • stable-diffusion.cpp

    Official

    Formats: gguf, safetensors. Memory policy: component stages stay resident.

    C/C++ runner with Metal on Mac and CUDA on NVIDIA. It reads GGUF and safetensors, and its docs keep a page per model family. Resident size is the sum of the weights, an upper bound.

    Sources: stable-diffusion.cpp README, backends

What does the official configuration say?

"Official Turbo settings are 8 steps, cfg 0.0 and mu 1.15, with generation from 1k to 2k resolution. No numeric RAM or VRAM minimum is given."

Source: Krea 2 README · Read 2026-10-24.

What known issues should you check?

  • Known issue 1

    The node author describes one 12.9B model as staying resident at about 18 to 20 GB with encoder and VAE. That is an estimate, not a measured peak.

    Source: ComfyUI-Krea2-MLX README · Read 2026-10-24

  • Known issue 2

    The Mac time comes from the node author README, with sampler, guidance and run date not stated. The source date is the commit that published it.

    Source: ComfyUI-Krea2-MLX README · Read 2026-10-24

Frequently asked questions

How fast is Krea 2 Turbo on a Mac?

The ComfyUI-Krea2-MLX author reports about 263 s for a 1024x1024 image in 8 steps with the mixed-4/8 build on an M1 Max with 32 GB. Sampler, guidance and run date are not stated, so the date shown is the README commit.

Can I use Krea 2 commercially?

Only below a revenue limit. The Krea 2 Community License allows commercial use when total company-wide annual revenue is under USD $1,000,000 on a trailing twelve-month basis. Above that you need an Enterprise License.

What is the difference between Krea 2 Turbo and Raw?

Turbo is the 8-step distilled checkpoint, with official settings of 8 steps and cfg 0.0. Raw is a separate undistilled checkpoint with its own 52-step settings, and Turbo results do not apply to it.
